truthAudit.Summary: Truth audit of Run 2 against 20 visible ground-truth vulnerabilities (SC-V3-001..SC-V3-020). Run 2 detected 10 of the 20 true vulnerabilities as real findings (SC-V3-001, 002, 004, 005, 006, 007, 009, 010, 011, 020), of which 4 required corrections to severity or CWE. Seven true vulnerabilities were entirely missed (SC-V3-003, 008, 012, 013, 014, 016, 017, 018, 019 — see items). Three additional findings in Run 2 were genuine issues but are not among the 20 ground-truth items (safe_string_copy off-by-one CWE-193, localtime CWE-479, timing comparison CWE-208) and are admitted as out-of-scope/false positives for this audit.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format String Vulnerability in log_debug_message | CWE-134 | Lines 237-238:\n        std::string active_format = runtime_log_format();\n        printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input);
Items.Notes: Run 2 correctly identified the runtime log format string passed to printf in log_debug_message (lines 237-238 of enhanced_calc.cpp). The quote matches the ground-truth anchors (runtime_log_format; printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input)). The CWE-134 classification is correct. Although Run 2 rated severity High vs. ground-truth Critical, that is a severity discrepancy recorded in corrections, not a detection-status overclaim.

Run 2 found the integer overflow in the fact lambda (lines 315-319), matching anchors result *= i and fact. CWE-190 is correct. Severity was rated Low vs. ground-truth High; the severity correction is recorded under corrections and does not count as a detection overclaim.

Run 2 did not identify the use-after-free caused by the stage_deferred_history_flush + memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() sequence in cleanup() (lines 881-884). Run 2's UAF finding was limited to the scratch lambda capturing a raw pointer without mentioning that cleanup() frees the pool immediately afterward, making the flush-lambda use-after-free the central issue. No quote from Run 2 links stage_deferred_history_flush to g_memory_pool.cleanup() as the UAF trigger.

Run 2 correctly identified command injection in validate_config via system(validator_cmd + " " + config_file). The quote matches anchors validator_cmd + " " + config_file; system(command.c_str()); admin validate. CWE-78 is correct. Severity High vs. ground-truth Critical is a severity correction recorded below, not a detection overclaim.

Run 2 correctly identified the stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression where strcpy copies an expression of length >= sizeof(input_buffer_) into the 1024-byte stack buffer. The quote matches anchors strcpy(input_buffer_; dest[src_len]; src_len > dest_size (the relevant branch). CWE-121 is acceptable. No correction needed.

Run 2 correctly identified the data race in ThreadSafeCounter::increment where the read of value_ occurs outside the lock. The quote matches anchors volatile long long; old_value = value_; lock_guard; value_ = old_value + 1. CWE-362 and Medium severity both match the ground truth. No correction needed.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Logic Bomb in Authentication | CWE-511 | if (login_attempts_ > 5) {\n                if (input.find("EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE") != std::string::npos) {\n                    authenticated_ = true;
Items.Notes: Run 2 correctly identified the logic bomb / bypass in authenticate() where login_attempts_ > 5 combined with EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE sets authenticated_ = true. The quote matches anchors login_attempts_ > 5; EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE; authenticated_ = true. CWE-511 and High severity match the ground truth. No correction needed.

Run 2 did not identify path traversal in ConfigLoader::load_config. The code concatenates config_dir_ + filename (line 543) and passes it directly to std::filesystem::exists / std::ifstream without sanitization, allowing path traversal. Run 2's command-injection finding for validate_config involved config file contents but did not flag path traversal in load_config. No quote from Run 2 addresses config_dir_ + filename or load_config path traversal.

Run 2 correctly identified the heap overflow in ExpressionParser::parse where a 256-byte heap buffer (expression_buffer_) is filled via unbounded strcpy. However, the CWE was listed as CWE-121 (stack buffer overflow) instead of the correct CWE-122 (heap buffer overflow), since the buffer is allocated from the memory pool, not the stack. The CWE correction is recorded below; detection of the vulnerability itself is credited.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Hardcoded Admin Secret | CWE-798 | Line 73:\n        constexpr char ADMIN_SECRET[] = "SC_ENT_2025_AUTH";
Items.Notes: Run 2 correctly identified the hardcoded administrator credentials ADMIN_SECRET / SC_ENT_2025_AUTH at line 73. The quote matches anchors ADMIN_SECRET; SC_ENT_2025_AUTH. CWE-798 is correct. Severity was rated Medium vs. ground-truth High; that discrepancy is recorded under corrections and is not a detection overclaim.

Run 2 correctly identified the weak PRNG for session tokens using std::mt19937 seeded by std::random_device with a uniform_int_distribution over 1000-9999. The quote matches anchors std::mt19937; uniform_int_distribution; 1000, 9999. CWE-338 is correct. Severity Medium vs. ground-truth High is a severity correction recorded below, not a detection overclaim.

Run 2 did not identify the thread-unsafe timestamp cache. Although Run 2 reported a 'Non-thread-safe localtime usage' finding, that finding cited CWE-479 (missing lock) and focused on localtime()'s static buffer, not the static std::tm cached_time that is written once and reused across threads (cached_time = *local_time). The ground-truth SC-V3-012 centers on the static cached_time timestamp cache pattern, which Run 2 did not report as its own finding.

Run 2 did not identify insecure temporary file handling as a distinct finding. Run 2's command-injection finding for append_override_audit_event framed the issue purely as command injection via environment-derived paths in a system() call (CWE-78). The ground-truth SC-V3-013 centers on insecure temporary file creation (TEMP/TMPDIR + supercalc_emergency.log written via shell redirection), which is a CWE-377 concern not captured by Run 2's framing. No quote from Run 2 addresses CWE-377 or insecure temp file creation.

Run 2 did not identify persistent authentication state. The code retains authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ in the AdminConsole object after authentication (lines 587-596), creating a CWE-613 issue. Run 2's authentication-related findings focused on timing comparison and the EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE bypass, not on the persistence of these state fields. No quote from Run 2 addresses authenticated_; login_attempts_; session_token_ persistence.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Non-thread-safe localtime usage | CWE-479 | Line 231:\n        if (auto* local_time = localtime(&time_t)) cached_time = *local_time;
Items.Notes: Run 2 did not identify unhandled exception in variable parsing (std::stod in handle_variable_command, line 729) as a finding. Run 2's localtime finding (CWE-479) is a genuine thread-safety issue but is not the ground-truth SC-V3-015. This item is recorded as a partial detection credit mismatch: the quote provided is Run 2's localtime finding, which does not match SC-V3-015's anchor (std::stod(tokens[3]); handle_variable_command).

Run 2 did not identify integer underflow in the memory-pool block split. The code computes previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES (lines 132-133) without guarding against underflow when previous_size is small. No quote from Run 2 addresses SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES, previous_size - size, or fragment.size = remaining.

Run 2 did not identify unbounded recursion in the parser. The recursive parse_expression -> parse_term -> parse_factor chain (with PAREN_OPEN calling parse_expression recursively at line 428) has no depth limit despite MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH being defined. No quote from Run 2 addresses parse_expression; parse_factor; PAREN_OPEN recursion.

Run 2 did not identify the data race in the result cache. ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached reads and writes result_cache_ (lines 446-450) without acquiring cache_mutex_, and is invoked via thread_pool_->enqueue (line 808). No quote from Run 2 addresses result_cache_; evaluate_cached; cache_mutex_; thread_pool_->enqueue.

Run 2 did not identify the TOCTOU vulnerability in ConfigLoader::load_config. The code checks std::filesystem::exists(full_path) at line 544, then sleeps for 25ms at line 545, then opens std::ifstream file(full_path) at line 546 — a classic TOCTOU window. No quote from Run 2 addresses std::filesystem::exists; sleep_for; std::ifstream file as a TOCTOU issue.

Run 2 correctly identified integer division by zero in calculate_route_score where token_length can be 0, leading to 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length). The quote matches anchors calculate_route_score; token_length; 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length). CWE-369 and Low severity both match the ground truth. No correction needed.
